profiles.summary: No opcode result differs from the specification at Monad/0.16.7 on 2026-11-26. The battery, the targeted set and script sets 1, 2 and 6 give the same results as in cycle 25. New this cycle: v0.16.7 is now released for mainnet, the Task 4 gas code read at v0.16.5 is unchanged at v0.16.7, the rewritten countl_zero of v0.16.6 reaches the PoolManager through its MULMOD sites with a 2^96 or 2^128 modulus and is correct, and three proposed MIPs add opcodes whose bytes the PoolManager bytecode does not contain outside push data.

deltas.delta: The releases page now lists v0.16.7 for mainnet on 2026-11-26 and for testnet on 2026-11-19. Cycle 25 read mainnet as N/A for this version. v0.16.6 carries the [EVM] entries for the once-per-element memory bound check, literal shifts as two unaligned loads, branchless CLZ and heap-independent block-exit stack writes.

From v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 the jsDelivr file hashes show x86.cpp and emitter.cpp changed, and runtime/call.cpp, runtime/storage.cpp and runtime/context.cpp unchanged. The x86.cpp diff adds only checked_debug_comment calls and a terminator_pc helper for them. In emitter.cpp the bodies of gas_decrement_static_work, gas_decrement_unbounded_work and accumulate_static_work hash the same at both tags (now lines 1054-1072 and 1305-1322). The Task 4 gas readings of cycle 26 therefore hold at v0.16.7.

countl_zero in uint256.hpp (v0.16.7 lines 1063-1074) is rewritten without early exit. bit_width (lines 1164-1168) uses it, and the emitter's modop_optimized (emitter.cpp 7774-7863) calls bit_width(m) - 1 to turn MULMOD with a literal power-of-two modulus into mul_mod2. The PoolManager bytecode has MULMOD with a PUSH13 2^96 modulus at pc 20958, 22639 and 22763 and a PUSH17 2^128 modulus at pc 22378; at pc 22721 a PUSH13 2^96 is pushed just before, but which operand it becomes was not traced. A transcription of the new countl_zero agrees with Python on 200,768 inputs and gives 96 and 128 for those moduli. mul_with_bit_size, which mul_mod2 calls for both widths, is byte equal between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7.

block_prologue (emitter.cpp 1340-1346 at v0.16.7) now rejects a block statically when max_delta - min_delta exceeds 1024, in place of the two separate bounds of v0.16.5. This is exactly the condition under which no entry stack size passes both runtime checks that follow, so it only moves an exceptional halt from run time to compile time.

MIP-7 (EXTENSION 0xAE), MIP-15 (Glamsterdam subset: EIP-7708, 7843 SLOTNUM, 7981, 7997, 8024 DUPN/SWAPN/EXCHANGE, 8246) and MIP-18 (CALLSTACKDEPTH and CALLERN under 0xAE) are in Review. Main's opcodes.hpp already gates DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE and SLOTNUM behind eip_8024_active and eip_7843_active. monad_mainnet.cpp on main still ends at MONAD_TEN and revision.h keeps MONAD_NEXT_AMSTERDAM unscheduled.

findings.title: MegaETH serves call results and balances at latest from mini-block state that the sequencer can still drop
findings.difference: On MegaETH the latest block selector returns the streaming state with committed mini-blocks. That state is ahead of the safe head, and finality depends on the containing EVM block being posted to and finalized on L1. On Ethereum, latest is a proposed block that a reorg can also drop, and OP Stack chains serve an unsafe head at latest as well. MegaETH differs in that latest includes mini-block state inside the current EVM block. The lead varies: two reads on 2026-11-26 gave 168 and 416 one-second blocks over safe, and 2,087 and 1,953 over finalized. Monad (F-153) and Avalanche (F-152) have the same class of hazard.
findings.mechanism: An integrator that reads a swap result, a take, or an ERC-6909 balance at latest and then acts off chain (pays out on another chain, releases goods) acts on state that only the sequencer has signed. If the sequencer drops or rewrites unsafe blocks, the PoolManager state rolls back with them. No PoolManager code path reads the selector; its accounting inside one transaction (PoolManager.sol:349-365 for settle, :291-297 for take) is unaffected. The hazard is the same shape as the Monad proposed-block finding of theme-deferred-verification and needs the operator to act.
findings.impact: Integrators that treat latest as final can be double spent by whoever controls the sequencer. LPs and claim holders inside the PoolManager lose nothing from this alone.
findings.preconditions: The sequencer drops or reorders unsafe blocks, and an off-chain party acted on latest.
findings.mitigations: Integrators wait for safe or finalized before acting off chain on PoolManager results.

cleared.result: The new loop keeps the value of the highest nonzero word and returns 256 for zero. A transcription agrees with Python on all powers of two, 2^k - 1, 2^k + 1 and 200,000 random words, and yields exponents 96 and 128. For both, last_ix is 1, so mul_mod2 inlines mul_with_bit_size, which is unchanged since v0.16.5 and ran natively in the cycle 23 harness.

cleared.check: Compiled paths for EXP with a literal power-of-two base, ADDMOD by mask and CLZ.
cleared.result: The deployed PoolManager on both networks and the build of this checkout contain no EXP, ADDMOD or CLZ instruction outside push data, so these emitter paths never run for it. Read anyway, the literal EXP path computes the shift count so that any exponent word of 2^32 or more gives zero, and the runtime-exponent path uses cmov on the original exponent when the product could overflow.

cleared.check: Upcoming Monad opcodes: MIP-7 EXTENSION (0xAE), MIP-15 DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE (0xE6-0xE8) and SLOTNUM (0x4B), and MIP-18 CALLSTACKDEPTH and CALLERN.
cleared.result: Neither the deployed PoolManager (eth_getCode on 143 and 4326, 24,009 bytes) nor the build has any of 0xAE, 0xE6, 0xE7, 0xE8, 0x4B or 0x1E as an instruction outside push data. MIP-7 and EIP-8024 keep JUMPDEST analysis unchanged. Activation therefore cannot change which jumps the PoolManager may take or what it computes. CALLERN only lets other contracts see ancestors; the PoolManager does not authorise by caller chain.

leads.question: When MONAD_NEXT_AMSTERDAM or a revision carrying MIP-15 or MIP-18 is scheduled in monad_mainnet.cpp, does the compiler's basic block parser on that tag treat the byte after 0xE6-0xE8 or 0xAE as part of the instruction when it splits blocks, and does any PoolManager jump target follow such a byte inside push data?
leads.why: The specifications keep JUMPDEST analysis unchanged, but the native compiler has its own block parser. The PoolManager has none of these bytes outside push data, so the question is only whether the parser respects push data on that tag.

leadResults.answer: MegaETH: yes. The selector reference says latest is the streaming state including committed mini-blocks, and on 2026-11-26 latest led safe by 168 blocks and finalized by 2,087. Recorded as an operator-level low finding. HyperEVM (999) is outside this unit and was not checked.
Not counted this cycle. The newest 5,942 MegaETH swaps were checked with swaps.py and replay.py and all match; the stateless-validator blocks were not enumerated.

The resource limits specification fetched on 2026-11-26 still says only 'sequencer-configured per-transaction gas cap'. The operations page gives an eth_call compute gas cap of 60,000,000 for the public gateway, which bounds simulation, not mined transactions.
Five whole pages (640 slots) of real PoolManager storage read the same through extsload and eth_getStorageAt at block 125,659,359 on rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com (Monad/0.16.7).

No native harness was run. By reading: at pc 20958 the PUSH13 2^96 is the second operand and the modulus comes from the stack, so the general runtime mulmod runs there (verifier's disassembly). The literal power-of-two moduli are at pc 22639 (2^96) and pc 22378 (2^128), where modop_optimized derives the exponent from the rewritten countl_zero, which is correct on 200,768 inputs, and mul_with_bit_size is unchanged since v0.16.5. The branch stays unreachable for ordinary accounts.
Operator-only ordering question; nothing new is public.
No public key-free Monad log index was searched this cycle; the sides it asks about remain covered by eth_call and harness runs of cycle 25.

No Monad tag after v0.16.7 exists on 2026-11-26 (jsDelivr versions list). On main, uint256.hpp is still 75,879 bytes and runtime/math.hpp still calls the division-based mulmod, so the Barrett code still reaches no opcode handler.
